source.title: My Neel Nanda MATS 10.0 Application: Studying Feature Splitting in SAEs via Training Data Attribution

record.file_problem: None; full post text is present, though some equations and symbols are missing in the web text.
record.tranche_reason: The study uses influence attribution and latent-pair measurements to investigate training-data effects on feature splitting dynamics, but does not compare SAE dictionary sizes or test the specific versions listed.
record.gate_note: Experiment 2's individual-latent attribution results (including Jaccard@200) are not rows because they do not test splitting. Experiment 1 computes pair metrics across 16,384 latents, but gives no aggregate outcome; the reported candidate pair example is recorded below. No results compare dictionary sizes, SAE families, or training objectives.
record.test_reason: The study uses a single Gemma Scope SAE (layer 3, 16k) and applies influence functions to latent pairs and individual latents. It never compares dictionary sizes, SAE families or objectives. It does not measure parent/child firing, absorption, or decomposition of larger-SAE latents. It redefines 'splitting' as similar latent pairs within one SAE and asks which training documents shape their decoder similarity. Its results do not bear on whether any version holds, so they are recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is mostly right. The executive summary is more positive than the paraphrase: it claims evidence that splitting and merging is shaped by specific documents, and that push documents induce same-token coactivation. The Results section, however, reports no evidence for the tested hypothesis. The influence functions yielded Jaccard@200 of 0.468 against max-activating documents, which the author treats with skepticism.
record.recipe_differences: Uses influence functions and qualitative latent-pair attribution on a single pretrained SAE, rather than comparing SAE dictionary sizes and measuring coarse-to-fine input coverage.

fits_no_version.finding: Influence functions find documents that increase or decrease decoder cosine similarity between latent pairs. The coactivation hypothesis was not supported overall; a few case studies show same-token coactivation in push documents.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Specific training documents shape the similarity of SAE latent pairs within a single SAE.

fits_no_version.finding: High-merge-score latent pairs with different autointerp labels can, on inspection, encode the same thing.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Within one SAE, near-duplicate latents with differing labels exist.

record.problems: The work uses one model and one SAE setting, a limited sample of Pile documents, small qualitative pair case studies, and no quantitative aggregate result for the pair coactivation hypothesis. The text also omits the displayed hypothesis and some equations.
record.rows_left_out: Experiment 1's full 16,384-latent metric scan is not separately recorded because the text gives no aggregate outcome for it. Experiment 2's individual-latent attribution results are omitted because they do not measure splitting.

untested.parts: No comparison across dictionary sizes; no coarse-to-fine coverage or direction measure.
One model, one SAE width and layer; no cross-scale or cross-family comparison.
No nested families or concept hierarchy examined.
No parent/child firing or absorption measurement; no variation of size or sparsity.
No comparison of latents between larger and smaller SAEs.
No objective comparison or Matryoshka SAEs; the role of training data is examined only qualitatively.

record.verdict_notes: This is an informal MATS application post with no peer review. 'Feature splitting' is redefined to include within-SAE and cross-run similarity, so the study does not engage the dictionary-size claim. Relation changed from 'tests' (T2) to 'discusses' (T6).

versions.untested_parts: Does not compare SAE dictionary sizes or test whether a larger dictionary replaces a coarse feature with finer features covering the same inputs and nearby directions.
Uses one Gemma-2-2B SAE setting; does not test large models or open SAE releases across scale.
Does not test nested feature families or whether a feature hierarchy mirrors the model's conceptual hierarchy.
Does not test parent-child latent firing, feature absorption, or whether changes to SAE size or sparsity resolve absorption.
Does not compare larger and smaller SAE latents or assess whether larger SAEs add novel latents.
Does not compare training objectives, test Matryoshka SAEs, or establish that splitting is an artifact of the SAE objective.
